architecture.design: Every OSI layer is an explicit node; protocols, PDUs, functions, mechanisms, parameters and interfaces connect directly to the layer they operate on or cross.

nodes.label: Layer 1 — Physical
nodes.description: Transmission/reception of raw bit streams and physical signal characteristics.

nodes.label: Layer 2 — Data Link
nodes.description: Node-to-node transfer, framing, error handling, connection and flow control.

nodes.label: Layer 3 — Network
nodes.description: Packet delivery across different networks, addressing, routing, traffic control, fragmentation.

nodes.label: Layer 4 — Transport
nodes.description: Host/application transfer, segmentation, reliability, flow/error control, QoS.

nodes.label: Layer 5 — Session
nodes.description: Management of communication sessions and continuous exchanges.

nodes.label: Layer 6 — Presentation
nodes.description: Data translation, character encoding, compression, encryption/decryption.

nodes.label: Layer 7 — Application
nodes.description: High-level network application services such as resource sharing and remote file access.

nodes.label: OSI Reference Model
nodes.description: Seven-layer reference model for communication systems.

nodes.label: ISO
nodes.description: International Organization for Standardization.

nodes.label: ITU-T
nodes.description: Telecommunications standardization body publishing X.200.

nodes.label: ISO/IEC 7498
nodes.description: Basic Reference Model standard.

nodes.label: ITU-T X.200
nodes.description: ITU-T version of the OSI reference model.

nodes.label: Host
nodes.description: Endpoint participating in communication.

nodes.label: Layer-N Peer Entity
nodes.description: Corresponding entity at the same layer on another host.

nodes.label: Communication Protocol
nodes.description: Rules enabling peer entities to communicate.

nodes.label: Layer Service
nodes.description: Functionality supplied by a lower layer to the layer above.

nodes.label: Protocol Data Unit
nodes.description: Layer-specific unit exchanged by peers.

nodes.label: Service Data Unit
nodes.description: Upper-layer PDU viewed as payload by the lower layer.

nodes.label: Protocol Header
nodes.description: Protocol metadata added during encapsulation.

nodes.label: Protocol Footer
nodes.description: Protocol metadata optionally added during encapsulation.

nodes.label: Encapsulation
nodes.description: Adding headers/footers as data moves downward.

nodes.label: Decapsulation
nodes.description: Removing headers/footers as data moves upward.

nodes.label: Peer Communication
nodes.description: Equivalent layer entities communicate as protocol peers.

nodes.label: Physical Transmission Medium
nodes.description: Physical medium carrying signals.

nodes.label: Network Address
nodes.description: Address used for network-layer delivery.

nodes.label: Routing
nodes.description: Selecting paths through intermediate nodes.

nodes.label: Fragmentation
nodes.description: Splitting oversized network messages.

nodes.label: Reassembly
nodes.description: Reconstructing fragments.

nodes.label: Segmentation
nodes.description: Splitting streams/large PDUs into smaller transport units.

nodes.label: Flow Control
nodes.description: Controls transmission rate between peers.

nodes.label: Error Control
nodes.description: Detects/handles transmission errors.

nodes.label: Acknowledgment
nodes.description: Confirms sequence/data existence.

nodes.label: Multiplexing
nodes.description: Shares transport service among application flows.

nodes.label: Quality of Service
nodes.description: Transport quality-of-service functions.

nodes.label: Connection-oriented
nodes.description: Transport service maintaining connection state.

nodes.label: Connectionless
nodes.description: Transport service without a persistent connection.

nodes.label: Maximum Transmission Unit
nodes.description: Maximum packet size supported along a path.

nodes.label: Maximum Segment Size
nodes.description: Maximum transport segment size after headers.

source_claims.claim: OSI is a seven-layer reference model.
Each layer serves the layer above and is served by the layer below.
Layer peers exchange PDUs through layer protocols.
Encapsulation adds headers/footers while moving downward.
Decapsulation strips headers/footers while moving upward.
Data link provides node-to-node transfer and link control.
Network layer provides multi-network delivery and routing.
Transport provides end-to-end/application transfer and QoS functions.
Security and management are cross-layer functions.
OSI does not define implementation-specific programming APIs.
TCP/IP mapping to OSI is approximate.
OSI was standardized through ISO/CCITT work and published in 1984.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: Layer is an architectural scope; protocol implements peer communication.
A PDU becomes an SDU when passed to the lower layer.
Sender adds metadata downward; receiver strips it upward.
Service describes functionality; protocol defines peer behavior.
Physical sends signals; link frames and controls directly connected nodes.
Link is node-to-node; network crosses different networks.
Network routes packets; transport manages application data sequences.
Session manages dialogs; transport manages end-to-end transfer.
Presentation translates data; application provides high-level services.
OSI explicitly has seven layers; TCP/IP uses broader functional scopes.
Some functions, especially security and management, span layers.
Conceptual architecture differs from the protocols originally designed for it.
Bit is logical information; signal is physical representation.
Transport may maintain connection state or not.

misconceptions.misconception: Every protocol fits cleanly in one layer.
misconceptions.correction: The source explicitly describes cross-layer functions and approximate mappings.

misconceptions.misconception: Every PDU is called a packet.
misconceptions.correction: OSI uses data, segment, packet/datagram, frame, and bit/symbol terminology.

misconceptions.misconception: Each layer is a separate physical device.
misconceptions.correction: Layers are abstractions that may be implemented across software and hardware.
It includes electrical/radio/optical signals, timing, modulation, connectors, and wireless parameters.
Network delivery need not be reliable.
The source includes multiple transport protocols and connection modes.

misconceptions.misconception: TCP/IP has a mandatory session layer.
misconceptions.correction: TCP/IP does not distinguish a separate session layer.
It also covers translation, encoding, and compression.

misconceptions.misconception: OSI and TCP/IP layers are identical.
misconceptions.correction: The source gives approximate mappings and important differences.

misconceptions.misconception: OSI protocols became the dominant Internet stack.
misconceptions.correction: TCP/IP became widespread while OSI protocols did not gain broad popularity.
